problem.claim: Characterize the parallel complexity of boosting, including the tradeoff between training rounds p and parallel work per round t, for nearly sample-optimal algorithms.

gap.claim: Existing parallel boosting algorithms fell short of established theoretical lower bounds across much of the p-versus-t tradeoff space.

contributions.claim: Provides improved lower bounds on the parallel complexity of weak-to-strong learners.
Introduces a parallel boosting algorithm whose performance matches the stated lower bounds across the full p-versus-t compromise spectrum up to logarithmic factors.
Reports settling the parallel complexity of boosting algorithms that are nearly sample-optimal.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish the work by jointly improving lower bounds and supplying a matching parallel boosting algorithm across the entire tradeoff spectrum, up to logarithmic factors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their algorithm matches the improved lower bounds across the entire p-versus-t spectrum up to logarithmic factors.
The authors report that the resulting bounds settle the parallel complexity of nearly sample-optimal boosting algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior work established strong round-versus-work lower bounds and algorithms covering different regions of the tradeoff.
The authors report closing the remaining gap with improved lower bounds and a matching algorithm across the full spectrum, up to logarithmic factors.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a lower-bound improvement with an algorithm claimed to match it across a stated parameter spectrum, while preserving the logarithmic-factor qualification.

lessons.interpretation: This creates direct alignment between the problem's theoretical limitation, the proposed construction, and the scope of the resolution.
lessons.application: When presenting a complexity result, explicitly pair the strengthened bound with a construction and state the exact parameter region and approximation-factor caveat.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work has no matching construction or when its guarantees apply only to isolated parameter regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal computational model, the exact lower-bound and algorithmic expressions, or the meaning of nearly sample-optimal.
The constants and dependence hidden by the logarithmic factors are not reported.
No experimental or empirical evaluation details are provided.
